title: Pick's theorem via primitive triangulation + GCD boundary count (Lean derivation)

problemStatement.formal: Given the primitive-triangulation result (PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.exists_primitive_triangulation: every lattice triangle T = (v_1, v_2, v_3) in (Z^2)^3 with |det(T)| > 0 decomposes into a List of |det(T)| primitive sub-triangles, each with |det| = 1) and the GCD boundary-count result (PicksTheoremOQ02.card_segmentPoints: the segment from (0,0) to (a,b) in N^2 contains exactly gcd(a,b) + 1 integer lattice points), can the formula Area(T) = I(T) + B(T)/2 - 1 -- where I(T) is the count of strictly-interior lattice points and B(T) = sum over edges of gcd(|Delta_x|, |Delta_y|) -- be derived constructively in Lean 4?
problemStatement.plain: Can Pick's theorem I + B/2 - 1 = Area be derived in Lean 4 by combining primitive triangulation (every triangle = |det| primitive pieces) with a boundary-point count via the GCD formula (lattice points on segment from v1 to v2 = gcd(|Dx|, |Dy|) + 1)?
whyMatters: Eliminates the axiom in Proofs/PicksTheorem.lean by deriving Pick's formula from already-verified ingredients.
Demonstrates the modularity of the Lean Genius proof library: independent results can be composed to retire axioms.
Provides a template for further Pick-style theorems (Ehrhart polynomial, n-dim Smith-normal-form bound) via the same primitive-decomposition + lattice-point-count strategy.

proven: Primitive triangulation (PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01.exists_primitive_triangulation): every non-degenerate lattice triangle decomposes into exactly |det| primitive pieces.
GCD boundary count (PicksTheoremOQ02.card_segmentPoints): the segment from (0,0) to (a,b) has gcd(a,b)+1 lattice points.
Pick's formula for axis-aligned rectangles (PicksTheoremOQ01, Part III).
open: Prove that EVERY primitive triangle (|det| = 1) has realInteriorCount = 0 (general base case, beyond the three test instances now verified in S2).
Prove the additivity lemma: when two lattice triangles T1, T2 share an edge with no interior lattice points (gcd = 1), realInteriorCount(T1 union T2) = realInteriorCount T1 + realInteriorCount T2.
knownResults.goal: Eliminate the picks_theorem axiom in PicksTheorem.lean by proving Pick's theorem for lattice triangles.

currentState.focus: Bridge primitive triangulation + GCD boundary count; S1 scaffold + S2 real-interior count + base-case agreement done.
currentState.nextAction: S3 -- prove the additivity lemma for primitive sub-triangles sharing a gcd=1 edge, or first the general primitive case (every twiceArea=1 triangle has realInteriorCount=0).

knowledge.progressSummary: S2 OBSERVE (researcher-4, 2026-05-12): extended Proofs/PicksTheoremOQ01OQ01OQ01.lean to 425+ lines (0 sorries, 0 axioms, build verified). Added cross2 (signed area cross product), LatticeTriangle.StrictInterior (Prop + Decidable instance), boundingBox (Finset.Icc x Finset.Icc), realInterior (filter on StrictInterior), realInteriorCount (the Finset cardinality), and proved by native_decide that realInteriorCount = pickInterior on the three test triangles (unit=0, 2x1=0, 3x3=1 with interior point (1,1)).
builtItems: cross2 (S2): twice the signed area of triangle (a, b, p) via the 2D cross product
LatticeTriangle.StrictInterior (S2): disjunction of two orientation cases on three edge cross products
Three test-triangle realInteriorCount theorems (S2): unitTriangle=0, triangle_2_1=0, triangle_3_3=1
Three test-triangle pick_agrees theorems (S2): (realInteriorCount : Q) = pickInterior
insights: Both ingredients (primitive triangulation + GCD boundary count) are already verified in the project; the bridge is purely compositional.
The cleared-denominator form pickInteriorNum = twiceArea - boundaryCount + 2 stays in Z, dodging the rationals during future induction proofs.
Each edge contributes gcd(|Dx|, |Dy|) + 1 lattice points; the three shared vertices double-count, so B = sum (gcd + 1) - 3 = sum gcd.
PicksTheoremOQ02 only handles segments from (0,0) to (a,b) with a, b : N; the general case needs a small translation/reflection lemma (still missing).
S2: The disjunction `(all > 0) OR (all < 0)` in StrictInterior covers both orientations of (v1, v2, v3), so we do not need to normalize the triangle's winding order.
S2: native_decide reduces realInteriorCount on any concrete triangle because Finset.Icc on Z, Finset.product, and the strict-interior predicate all compile to decidable computations.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has Convex / intrinsicInterior for topological interiors but no built-in lattice-point-of-triangle count; we use a custom Finset.Icc + filter definition (S2).
Mathlib.Data.Int.Interval is required for Finset.Icc on Z (LocallyFiniteOrder Z); Mathlib.Data.Finset.Prod for Finset.product.
nextSteps: S3a (prep): Prove the GENERAL primitive case -- every LatticeTriangle T with T.twiceArea = 1 has T.realInteriorCount = 0 (closes the base case beyond the three test instances).
S3b: Prove the additivity lemma for primitive-edge unions (gcd = 1 case): realInteriorCount(T1 ∪ T2) = realInteriorCount T1 + realInteriorCount T2 + (boundary points on the shared edge).
